# 3am-plugins

Personal Claude Code plugin marketplace.

## Prerequisites

- **Python** (3.10+)
- **uv** — script execution (`pip install uv` or `brew install uv`)
- **Task** — task runner (optional, for local development)

## Quick start

One-liner setup:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brianclaridge/3am-plugins/main/setup.sh | bash
```

Or manually in a Claude Code session:

```bash
# 1. Register the marketplace
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/brianclaridge/3am-plugins.git

# 2. Browse available plugins
/plugin > Discover

# 3. Install a plugin
/plugin install <name>@3am
```

## Available plugins

| Plugin | Description |
|---|---|
| [bootstrap](plugins/bootstrap/) | Sync all plugins from this marketplace |
| [insights](plugins/insights/) | Generate themed usage insights reports from Claude Code session data |
| [figma](plugins/figma/) | Figma MCP integration for design-to-code and code-to-design workflows |
| [statusline](plugins/statusline/) | Custom ANSI status line with session metrics, usage bars, and themes |

See [`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`](.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) for the full plugin index.

## Bootstrap

Sync everything in one shot:

```text
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/brianclaridge/3am-plugins.git
/plugin install bootstrap@3am
/sync
```

The `/sync` command fetches the marketplace index and walks you through installing every available plugin.

## Docs

- [Plugin authoring reference](docs/CLAUDE_PLUGINS.md)
- [Marketplace & distribution reference](docs/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE.md)

## References

### Figma

- [Claude Code to Figma: Turning Production Code into Editable Figma Designs](https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-claude-code-to-figma/)
- [Introducing our MCP server: Bringing Figma into your workflow](https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-figma-mcp-server/)
- [Guide to the Figma MCP server](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/32132100833559-Guide-to-the-Figma-MCP-server)
- [Tools and prompts — Figma MCP server](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/tools-and-prompts/)

# bootstrap

Sync all plugins from the 3am marketplace with a single command.

## Install

```text
/plugin install bootstrap@3am
```

## Usage

```text
/sync
```

Fetches the marketplace index, lists all available plugins, and walks you through installing each one.

## Auto-sync

Bootstrap includes a **SessionStart hook** that automatically detects missing marketplace plugins at the start of every session. If any plugins from `3am` are not installed, the hook injects a system message telling Claude to install them before doing anything else.

- **Silent when synced** — produces zero output when all plugins are already installed
- **User-scope recommended** — install bootstrap at user scope so auto-sync works across all projects
- **Manual sync still available** — run `/sync` at any time for a full bulk install

# insights

Generate themed usage insights reports from Claude Code session data. Produces a self-contained HTML report styled with a GitHub Dark theme.

## Install

```
/plugin install insights@3am
```

## Usage

```
/insights
```

The command reads session data from `~/.claude/usage-data/facets/` and `session-meta/`, aggregates stats, and writes a timestamped HTML report to `.data/claude/insights/` in your current project directory.

Requires the built-in `/insights` command to have run at least once to generate the raw JSON data files.

## Output

Reports are saved as `.data/claude/insights/{YYMMDD}_{HHMMSS}_claude_insights.html` and can be opened directly in a browser.

# figma

Figma MCP integration for design-to-code and code-to-design workflows.

## Install

```text
/plugin install figma@3am
```

## What it does

Installs the plugin and **auto-registers the remote Figma MCP server** (`https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`) via `.mcp.json`. No manual `claude mcp add` needed.

Once connected, you get access to Figma's 13 MCP tools — design context extraction, screenshot capture, design generation, variable definitions, Code Connect mapping, and more.

## Usage

After installing, Figma tools are available in any Claude Code session. Ask Claude to:

- Generate a Figma design from a description or code
- Extract design tokens and variables from a Figma file
- Take screenshots of Figma frames
- Map Figma components to your codebase with Code Connect

## Setup command

```text
/figma-setup
```

Guided setup that walks you through:

- **Status check** — verify the MCP server is responding
- **Transport switch** — switch to the desktop server for selection-based prompting
- **Project init** — generate design system rules tailored to your tech stack
- **Code Connect** — map Figma components to your code

# statusline

Custom ANSI status line for Claude Code with session metrics, usage bars, git info, team/task progress, account stats, and extensible token providers.

## What it shows

- **Session info** — model name, cost, duration, lines added/removed
- **Context window** — usage bar with color tiers (green/yellow/red)
- **Git info** — branch, short SHA, dirty/clean, staged/unstaged/untracked counts, ahead/behind, last commit
- **Session details** — session ID, cache read/write tokens, plan name, cwd
- **Usage API bars** — session, weekly, sonnet, opus, cowork, extra usage with reset timers
- **Team progress** — active team tasks bar with agent count
- **Account stats** — today's activity, lifetime totals, account email
- **Custom providers** — extend with your own tokens via standalone scripts

## Install

```text
/plugin install statusline@3am
```

`setup.sh` auto-configures `~/.claude/settings.json` with the statusline command. To reconfigure manually or change scope, run `/statusline:3am`.

Requires [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for script execution.

## Themes

Two built-in themes: **default** and **cyberpunk**. Set the `theme:` key in your config file.

## Config override chain

Highest priority first:

1. `STATUSLINE_CONFIG` env var — absolute path to a config file
2. `.claude/statusline.yml` — project-level override
3. `~/.config/3am/statusline.yml` — user-level override
4. Bundled `statusline.yml` in the plugin — default

## Providers

Providers are standalone `.py` scripts that receive context via stdin JSON and return `{token_name: rendered_string}` via stdout JSON. They run as subprocesses — fully isolated, a crash never affects the statusline.

Discovery chain (higher priority wins on filename collision):

1. `STATUSLINE_PROVIDERS_DIR` env var
2. `.claude/statusline-providers/` in the project
3. `~/.config/3am/statusline-providers/`

## Architecture

```text
scripts/
  statusline.py              # thin uv-run-script runner
  statusline/
    __main__.py               # orchestration, multi-TTL cache loop
    cache.py                  # JSON cache for throttling redraws
    config.py                 # paths, constants, YAML config loading
    git_info.py               # git subprocess calls
    payload_log.py            # debug payload logger
    providers.py              # subprocess-based token providers
    render.py                 # ANSI rendering helpers
    session_info.py           # ~/.claude.json session reader
    task_info.py              # team/task scanner
    tokens.py                 # token builder (all data sources)
    usage_api.py              # Usage API client
```

# tmux

Manage tmux pane layouts from Claude Code. Detects current orientation, rearranges panes, and shows keybindings.

## Commands

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `/tmux` | Show current pane status |
| `/tmux fix` | Arrange panes side by side |
| `/tmux stacked` | Stack panes top/bottom |
| `/tmux tiled` | Tile all panes evenly |

## How it works

A PEP 723 Python script (`tmux_ctl.py`) wraps `tmux list-panes` and `tmux select-layout` with structured JSON output and friendly layout aliases.

tmux's naming is counterintuitive — `even-vertical` means vertical **dividers** (panes side by side), not vertical panes. The skill handles this translation.

## Requirements

- tmux running in the terminal
- `uv` for script execution
